scope: Read-only visual/UX inspection of7 current native game screens; no production code changes.
fixture: Local Vite5191 / PGlite54322 native SQL fixture rooms; separate KO and ES contexts; manual refresh because fixture has noRealtime. Not a live commercial-service test.

findings.quality: Readable tile material and numerals; oversized panel hierarchy makes this feel like a dashboard rather than a compact deduction table.
findings.state: Initial hand preparation; current setup phase own rack is visible at KO 1440×900. Previous active-phase screenshot had rack below the fold and is not used as current-state proof.
issues: Board begins y194 KO / y296 ES. Two nearly full-width racks hold only four left-aligned tiles, leaving most of their panel area empty.
Large header, phasebar and standalone setup message compete with the tiles. Board ends y936 KO, beyond viewport.
findings.direction: Charcoal deduction desk: opposing centered tile rails around one compact central guess tray; compact score/phase ribbon, contextual controls beside selected tile.

findings.quality: Strongest usable initial composition: main task and chat are both visible, but word selection reads as a generic white form.
findings.state: Word-selection phase only; drawing, guesses and reward transition not captured.
issues: Three word cards are plain outlined text rectangles with minimal illustration or personality.
The same two scores appear in top score strip and side round status. Blank space dominates preparation panel.
Tiny instruction/status labels lack a clear second-level type hierarchy.
findings.direction: Warm artist studio: large paper canvas, one compact palette/tool rail, playful hand-drawn word cards, chat as a narrow shared notebook.

findings.quality: Tile material and felt are plausible; oversized informational cards and owner setup panel dominate the playable area.
findings.state: Initial round; KO owner configuration shown, ES guest configuration collapsed.
issues: KO initial board height1172; own playable hand is below viewport while 6 setup selects fill its bottom.
Duplicated full-width team summary and seat panels consume about175px before the felt.
ES own tiles look washed out while waiting; distinction between disabled and readable physical tiles needs improvement.
findings.direction: Dominican club table: center continuous felt with compact opponent/team badges around perimeter; own ivory tiles docked at bottom; configuration collapsed in one control after room setup.

findings.quality: Consistent warm palette and goods silhouettes; card faces resemble oversized icon dashboard panels and delay access to the actual hand and token supply.
issues: Market faces are hard-coded230px high; own hand starts aroundy863 KO and y951 ES.
Supply/token collection is below the visible screen in both viewports.
Repeated rounded ivory shells (scores, market, opponent, hand, herd, supply) flatten hierarchy and lose the tabletop focus.
Camel/goods art is internally coherent but simple isolated SVG icons leave large blank card areas; a more authored card face system needs artwork and card framing, not only CSS shades.
findings.direction: Illustrated desert bazaar: compact portrait goods cards with full card composition, market and hand in neighboring rows, six tangible token stacks on a lateral supply rail.

findings.quality: Actual illustrated card faces materially improve quality, but the interaction shells prevent the complete market from being scanned in one view.
findings.state: Initial market, nobles and bank; no purchase/reward capture.
issues: Board height1546 KO /1399 ES; only top tier fully fits KO1440×900, bottom tier and treasury are not visible in either viewport.
Each market tier is about260–300px high because every card carries a bonus label and action tray underneath.
Noble portraits repeat their printed requirements using adjacent HTML gem chips; development card costs are printed only and are NOT duplicated in HTML.
Bank token drawings are thin outlined circular controls beside richer photographic card art; materials do not match within this game.
findings.direction: Renaissance jeweler tabletop: all three4-card tier rows simultaneously visible, portrait noble tiles across top, tactile gem stacks on right, acquisition/reservation tray below; card actions reveal on selection.

findings.quality: Distinct pawns and40-space layout are recognizable, but small repeated city thumbnails and dense microtext compete with navigation around a partially clipped board.
findings.state: Initial pawn selection/roll panel; no movement/reward capture.
issues: Board height1075 KO /1113 ES; lower perimeter spaces fall below visible viewport.
A six-option pawn selection panel occupies the board center while center/table itself extends beyond the screen.
City thumbnails are small with no strong city or region identity; price/rent/name/flag/art all compete in a narrow tile.
Owner action column is readable but needs a clear purchase/rent/balance hierarchy when the board is fit to screen.
findings.direction: Bright illustrated travel board: square viewport-fit perimeter, flat legible tile faces with one city motif each, large animated pawn movement, one contextual action drawer at side; pawn chooser closes after selection.

findings.quality: Consistent48-card art and flattened individual field cards are a meaningful improvement; the stacked board composition still hides the hand actions and collection.
findings.state: Current native initial deal after Luna flattening and capturable hand highlights; scoring/Godori changes were in progress around capture time.
issues: Board starts y194 KO and ends y1200; hand starts abouty730, while both capture racks are lower than viewport.
Field rows, reveal help, centered dealt-event pill, phase message, hand area, event history, capture racks and scoring disclosure are vertically serialized.
Thick wooden/brown surrounds consume more space than a compact game table needs. Capture categories are only visible after scrolling away from the actual playable hand.
Hand month labels are embedded in card art; some card identities would benefit from clear accessible categorization without expanding per-card chrome.
findings.direction: Classic Korean hwatu table: large central green field with ten-card hand docked below; compact opposing score rails; capture categories on two side rails; reveal/reward temporarily presented on the table where capture occurs.

sharedFindings: All boards start at y194 in KO1440×900 and y296 in ES1920×1080. ES wider viewport preserves more top spacing rather than gaining proportional play space.
No initial captures show horizontal page overflow or broken images; these are implementation checks, not evidence of commercial visual quality.
Five games except Catchmind and initial-setup DaVinci hide major game areas below the screen. Finishing gradients or borders cannot solve this composition gap.
Visual identity may differ between games; consistency is required within each game between art, tokens, card faces, control materials and state presentation.

acceptanceChecks.name: Desktop composition
acceptanceChecks.criteria: At KO1440×900 and ES1920×1080, viewport includes player hand, central public board, primary action and both score/turn states without page scroll. Optional rules/logs/settings may scroll or collapse.

acceptanceChecks.name: Playable focus
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Global and room/game chrome together use no more than150px at both target viewports; no repeated full-size game title or duplicate score panels.

acceptanceChecks.name: Full market and collections
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Splendor shows all12 development cards and3 nobles plus bank/treasury; Jaipur shows5 market cards, up to7 hand cards and6 supply stacks; Minhwatu shows current field, hand and both capture category summaries; Marble shows all40 perimeter spaces.

acceptanceChecks.name: Readable materials
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Core card identifiers/resources/amounts remain readable at screenshot100%; essential labels at least12px, important numbers at least16px; card art keeps natural aspect ratio and decoded images.

acceptanceChecks.name: Control legibility
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Primary turn control has44px target; unavailable actions remain readable but visually secondary. Keyboard focus/selected target differs visibly from merely playable state.

acceptanceChecks.name: Art coherence
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Each game has one approved direction for faces, backs, tokens, board and controls. Review actual full screen at100% and object close-up; no emoji placeholder main game pieces or unexplained generic icon card fronts.

acceptanceChecks.name: Reward presentation
acceptanceChecks.criteria: Capture, sale, purchase, correct guess, domino score and marble rent each visibly identify the affected object and confirmed amount, then settle into persistent board/collection state; verify both actor and partner/reduced-motion paths using actual confirmed actions.

limitations: Initial native states only for all7; no bounded capture of current active DaVinci guesses, Catchmind drawing, or any reward/terminal state in this audit. Reward checks are proposed criteria, not passing results.
No mobile, accessibility contrast calculation, live Supabase/Realtimes, full game playtest, or new artwork review. Existing passing unit/integration tests do not validate commercial visual quality.
Minhwatu source was changing during the session; final consolidated composition implementation is deliberately deferred to next session per request to push repository.
